verdicts.claim: A checkpoint moves the transactions in the WAL file back into the main database file. SQLite runs one automatically when a COMMIT leaves the WAL at 1000 pages
verdicts.evidence: wal.html 3.1: 'automatically checkpoint whenever a COMMIT occurs that causes the WAL file to be 1000 pages or more in size, or when the last database connection on a database file closes'; sec 6: 'about 1000 pages (and is thus about 4MB'; SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT named.

verdicts.claim: Automatic checkpointing is on by default with a 1000-page threshold... A value of 0 or a negative value disables it.
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: 'Setting the auto-checkpoint size to zero or a negative value turns auto-checkpointing off... All automatic checkpoints are PASSIVE... enabled by default with an interval of 1000'.

verdicts.claim: PASSIVE mode copies as many frames as it can without waiting... FULL... RESTART... TRUNCATE truncates the WAL file to zero bytes just before it returns
verdicts.evidence: wal_checkpoint_v2 page defines all four modes as stated, incl. 'truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to a successful return'.

verdicts.claim: Every checkpoint takes an exclusive checkpoint lock; if another connection is already checkpointing, the call returns SQLITE_BUSY immediately
verdicts.evidence: v2 page: 'All calls obtain an exclusive "checkpoint" lock... SQLITE_BUSY is returned. Even if there is a busy-handler configured, it will not be invoked'; FULL/RESTART/TRUNCATE 'also obtain the exclusive "writer" lock'.

verdicts.claim: A checkpoint can run concurrently with readers but must stop at the first WAL page past any active reader's end mark; it records progress in the wal-index
verdicts.evidence: wal.html 2.2: 'must stop when it reaches a page in the WAL that is past the end mark of any current reader... remembers (in the wal-index) how far it got'; 'a long-running read transaction can prevent a checkpointer from making progress'.

verdicts.claim: A normal checkpoint does not shrink the WAL file... journal_size_limit (default -1...; 0 means always truncate to the minimum size)... set separately for each attached database
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: 'default journal size limit is -1 (no limit)'; 'To always truncate... set the journal_size_limit to zero'; 'This pragma only operates on the single database specified'.

verdicts.claim: When the last connection closes cleanly, SQLite checkpoints and deletes the -wal and -shm files unless SQLITE_FCNTL_PERSIST_WAL is set.
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'that connection does one last checkpoint and then deletes the WAL and its associated shared-memory file'; retained 'if the SQLITE_FCNTL_PERSIST_WAL file control is used'.

verdicts.claim: NOOP mode copies no frames. Its only use is to read the WAL size (*pnLog) and the number of frames already checkpointed. After a successful TRUNCATE, both 0
verdicts.evidence: v2 page: 'The only reason to invoke a NOOP checkpoint is to access the values...'; 'upon successful completion of an SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE... both *pnLog and *pnCkpt will be set to zero'.

verdicts.claim: PRAGMA wal_checkpoint returns one row: busy flag (1 if a FULL, RESTART or TRUNCATE checkpoint was blocked), number of WAL pages, pages checkpointed; -1 if not WAL
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: 'returns a single row with three integer columns... 1 if a RESTART or FULL or TRUNCATE checkpoint was blocked... second and third column are -1 if there is no write-ahead log'.

verdicts.claim: Litestream disables application auto-checkpoints (recommends PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint = 0), holds a read lock... busy_timeout (5000 ms suggested)
verdicts.evidence: tips: 'maintaining a read lock on the database in between its checkpoint requests'; 'PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint = 0;'; 'requires periodic but short write locks'; 'PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000;'.

verdicts.claim: Litestream v0.5.x runs checkpoints in three tiers... truncate-page-n (default 121359 pages, about 500 MB)... passive-first in v0.5.15... checkpoint-interval 1m
verdicts.evidence: guide: 'truncate-page-n: 121359 # Default : ~500MB'; 'Passive-first truncation v0.5.15'; 'min-checkpoint-page-count: 1000 # Default : ~4MB'; 'checkpoint-interval: 1m'; long-read apps 'Set truncate-page-n: 0' with disk monitoring.

verdicts.claim: Checkpoint frequency is a trade-off... the 1000-page default is tuned for workstation tests only.
verdicts.evidence: wal.html 2.3 states the read/write trade-off and 'this strategy seems to work well in test applications on workstations, but other strategies might work better'; 'tuned for workstation tests only' is a mild overstatement of that wording.

verdicts.claim: Checkpoints cost more than write transactions because they must sync the WAL before copying and sync the database file before reset. With synchronous=NORMAL
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'The WAL must be synced... prior to moving content... database file must be synced prior to resetting the WAL'; 'with PRAGMA synchronous set to NORMAL, the checkpoint is the only operation to issue an I/O barrier'; main thread 'will never block on a sync operation'.

verdicts.claim: With PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL the checkpoint is the only operation that issues a sync... at the cost of durability across power loss.
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'transactions are no longer durable and might rollback following a power failure'; Litestream tips: fsync 'only called when the WAL becomes full and has to checkpoint'.

verdicts.claim: Litestream keeps a long-running read transaction open so that no other process can checkpoint and restart the WAL. Litestream then runs the checkpoints itself
verdicts.evidence: how-it-works: 'starts a long-running read transaction to prevent any other process from checkpointing and restarting the WAL file... manually calls out to SQLite to perform checkpoints'.

verdicts.claim: Checkpoint starvation: if there is always at least one overlapping reader, no checkpoint completes and the WAL file grows without bound. SQLite recommends 'reader gaps'
verdicts.evidence: wal.html sec 6: 'always at least one active reader, then no checkpoints will be able to complete and hence the WAL file will grow without bound'; 'reader gaps'; RESTART/TRUNCATE 'readers might block'.

verdicts.claim: Disabling auto-checkpoint without running manual checkpoints is an antipattern... since 3.11.0 the WAL size for one transaction is proportional
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'If an application disables the automatic checkpoint, then there is nothing to prevent the WAL file from growing excessively'; 'As of SQLite version 3.11.0 (2016-02-15), the WAL file for a single transaction should be proportional in size'.

verdicts.claim: Separating a database from its WAL can lose committed transactions or corrupt the database. The only safe way to remove a leftover WAL is sqlite3_open()
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'transactions that were previously committed... might be lost, or the database file might become corrupted. The only safe way to remove a WAL file is to open the database file using one of the sqlite3_open() interfaces then immediately close'.

verdicts.claim: In FULL, RESTART and TRUNCATE modes, if the busy handler gives up..., the checkpoint continues as a PASSIVE one and returns SQLITE_BUSY
verdicts.evidence: v2 page: 'If the busy-handler returns 0 before the writer lock is obtained or while waiting for database readers, the checkpoint operation proceeds... in the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE... SQLITE_BUSY is returned'.

verdicts.claim: The WAL-reset bug... likely present from 3.7.0 (2010) through 3.51.2. SQLite fixed it in 3.51.3 (2026-03-13), with backports 3.44.6 and 3.50.7
verdicts.evidence: wal.html sec 11: 'likely present in all version of SQLite from 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2 (2026-01-09). It is fixed in version 3.51.3 (2026-03-13)... Backports... 3.44.6 and 3.50.7'; consensus.dev shows both lost writes and corruption.

verdicts.claim: Disagreement: sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2 page says RESTART 'does not impede readers'... wal.html says 'readers might block while the checkpoint is running'
verdicts.evidence: Both quotes present verbatim: v2 page 'blocks new database writer attempts while it is pending, but does not impede readers'; wal.html 'readers might block while the checkpoint is running'.

verdicts.claim: Overview: Tools such as Litestream take over checkpointing themselves.
verdicts.evidence: how-it-works: 'Litestream works by effectively taking over the checkpointing process'.
